t:
(a) Designation.—The outpatient clinic of the Department of Veterans Affairs located in Farmington, Missouri, shall be known and designated as the “Robert Silvey Department of Veterans Affairs Outpatient Clinic”.  
    (b) References.—Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the facility referred to in subsection (a) shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Robert Silvey Department of Veterans Affairs Outpatient Clinic”.

fable.w: This section only names a VA outpatient clinic and tells readers how to interpret references to it in federal records. The tempting reading is that the word "regulation" in subsection (b) signals rulemaking, but it is only boilerplate listing existing records in which the facility's name is deemed updated. No party outside the federal government is consulted or given any role in a federal decision.
fable.s: shall be known and designated as the “Robert Silvey Department of Veterans Affairs Outpatient Clinic”

qwen_block.w: This section merely renames a federal facility. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. There are no advisory boards, public hearings, or opportunities for outside input mentioned.
qwen_block.s: (a) Designation.—The outpatient clinic of the Department of Veterans Affairs located in Farmington, Missouri, shall be known and designated as the “Robert Silvey Department of Veterans Affairs Outpatient Clinic”.

opus.w: This section only names a VA outpatient clinic and makes references to the facility use the new name. It involves no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. The word "regulation" is standard boilerplate about existing records, not a grant of rulemaking authority, so it does not count as participation.
opus.s: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the facility referred to in subsection (a) shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Robert Silvey Department of Veterans Affairs Outpatient Clinic”.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through.** The only tempting hook is the word "regulation" in subsection (b), which could be mistaken for a grant of rulemaking authority. That reading fails. The clause only says that existing references in records of the United States now point to the new name. It gives no one power to issue rules and brings in no one from outside the federal government. The section just names a VA facility, so no outside party takes part in any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section simply designates a specific Department of Veterans Affairs outpatient clinic with a new name. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or participation by parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or experts) in making a federal decision. The action is a unilateral legislative act naming a facility, which falls outside the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that naming a facility after a person involves some form of public recognition or consultation, but the text itself contains no procedural requirement for outside parties to participate in the decision to name the clinic. It is a unilateral legislative designation.
